A sweep holding a price-target watch runs every sweep_priority_interval_seconds, the rest every sweep_interval_seconds; price bands (each price_alerts rule: price_band_query, Buy It Now, between the floor and the target) every price_band_interval_seconds catch OLD listings cut under a target; they only ever raise target pings. Full passes of every watch's own queries run in the remaining request budget. Terms are names every genuine title carries (eBay returns NOTHING past ~10 OR alternatives: 10 worked, 12 gave 0 results on 2026-10-18); measure changes with corpus.yml ab_mode=sweeps. 2026-10-21: eBay itself shows a new listing in search ~3.2 min after it goes live (tools/fresh_probe.py: same for every URL variant, no cache to bust), so the monitor's own share is the wait for the next sweep; 4 groups, all every 30 s, keep that ~30 s for every watch (6 groups at 30/60 s left the 60 s ones ~55 s behind, the request budget running ~5 sweeps a minute).
